title: Hark! Through the Waking Earth
description: Hark! Through the Waking Earth in Tonic Solfa to QUAM DILECTA, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 188, “Behold, He Cometh”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes (6.6.6.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to QUAM DILECTA; any other Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! through the wa-king earth, Hark! through the e-choing sky, Her-ald of free-dom's birth, There comes a glo-rious cry.

lines: Sound, sound through all the earth!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to QUAM DILECTA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
